This conclusion moves the competitive dimension of memory systems from the technical implementation layer to the architecture philosophy layer. Any system that implements the write–manage–read closed loop will not find capacity to be the bottleneck—the bottleneck is whether the governance logic at each stage is sound. The shift in evaluation direction (from recall to update/abstain/drift/selective forget) means: future memory system evaluation will no longer focus only on storage volume and recall rate, but on whether the system can proactively discard certain memories at the right time, determine whether a belief is outdated, and choose not to invoke a memory in the face of uncertainty. 864bsk:275: The four models (user, task, world, self) do not exist independently; the coupling relationships among them are where the real value lies. The intersection of the user model and the world model determines preference applicability—when the user says "I like microservices," the validity of that preference within a particular organizational structure depends on that organization's service-boundary governance capability. The intersection of the task model and the self model determines the Agent's self-calibration ability—knowing which paths have failed before allows it to actively avoid them during planning. The "intent" that emerges from this multi-model coupling is actually a high-dimensional latent variable that cannot be directly observed and can only be approximated through long-term collaboration of multiple models. This explains why traditional key-value memory systems have never been able to produce reliable intent understanding—they lack a dynamic coupling layer between models.

dosamf:227: RAG-style semantic-similarity retrieval assumes "surface semantic relevance = substantive relevance." But truly valuable memory recall is often counterintuitive. A Black Friday traffic problem from three months ago determines today's cache design constraints—yet these two pieces of information are far apart in semantic space. Task-constraint-driven retrieval-inference coupling essentially asks: which variables constrain the current decision? What source memories do these constraints come from?
